title: Orchestration task record
description: One record in the durable task manifest engagements/<session>/runs/tasks.jsonl. The manifest is append-only JSONL — the latest record for a given task_id is the current state. A task is the unit of work keyed by (agent, subscription_id, check_id, scope_hash); this lets a long run resume (skip 'done' tasks, retry 'failed'/'throttled'), enforce budgets, write to per-task output paths, and turn a partial/failed task into a recorded coverage gap instead of aborting the whole engagement. See knowledge/scaling.md -> 'Orchestration at scale'.

task_id.description: Deterministic identifier: <agent>:<subscription_id>:<check_id>:<scope_hash[0:8]>. Stable across re-runs so the manifest is idempotent.

agent.description: Domain agent that owns the task, e.g. network-exposure.

subscription_id.description: Subscription the task runs against (a subscription is the unit of work; multi-sub runs are fan-out).

check_id.description: The check the task executes, e.g. nsg-mgmt-port-open-internet.

scope_hash.description: Hash over the canonical (agent, subscription_id, check_id, scope) tuple. Distinguishes the same check run against different scope parameters.

status.description: pending=not started; running=in flight; done=completed; failed=errored (retryable); throttled=hit rate limit (retryable); partial=completed with a recorded coverage gap (e.g. paging/budget cut short); skipped=intentionally not run (scope/budget).

attempts.description: Number of times this task has been started. Drives retry/backoff decisions on resume.

output_refs.description: Per-task output paths (e.g. findings/raw/<agent>/<subscription>/<check>.jsonl). Each task writes its OWN files; a deterministic reduce step merges them. Parallel workers never append to one shared file.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation for failed / skipped / partial / throttled statuses. Becomes the coverage-gap reason.
